providers.title: Monotone coupling
providers.scope: For an increasing family F, p -> mu_p(F) is a nondecreasing polynomial, strictly increasing from 0 to 1 when F is nontrivial.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Unions of independent product sets
providers.scope: A union of independent mu_(p_i)-random sets is mu_(p*)-random with 1 - p* = prod (1 - p_i), and p* <= sum p_i.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Expectation thresholds
providers.scope: q(F) <= q_f(F) <= p_c(F) for every nontrivial increasing family F.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spread members
providers.scope: If a random member A of F satisfies P(J in A) <= sigma^|J| for nonempty J, then q(F) <= q_f(F) <= sigma.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Counting copies
providers.scope: M(F) = (n)_v(F) / |Aut F|, and a uniformly random copy of I contains a fixed copy of F with probability M(I,F)/M(F).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The expectation threshold of a graph
providers.scope: p_E(n,H) is determined by the nonempty edge subsets of H, satisfies 0 < p_E(n,H) <= p_c(n,H), and ignores isolated vertices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graph and abstract expectation thresholds
providers.scope: p_E(n,H) <= q(F_H) <= q_f(F_H) <= p_c(n,H).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Expectation threshold of a perfect matching
providers.scope: 1/(2n) <= p_E(n, PM_n) <= e^2/n for every even n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Isolated vertices
providers.scope: For n >= 16, G(n, log n/(3n)) has an isolated vertex with probability greater than 1/2; hence p_c(n, PM_n) > log n/(3n).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fractional threshold of a perfect matching
providers.scope: q(F_PM_n) <= q_f(F_PM_n) <= e^2/n for every even n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Overlaps of a spread family
providers.scope: For an a-spread family and a label of size at most m, P(|A_c intersect A_b| = r) <= binom(m,r) a^r.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Planting
providers.scope: If W ~ mu_rho is independent of the source, Y = W union A_c has density Z with respect to mu_rho, the target is a posterior sample, and P(Z(Y) < theta) <= theta.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local resampling (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For an a-spread family with labels of size at most m and a <= e^(-50) rho, a local failure has probability at most e^(-9m), and the event that the target is b changes the law of W outside A_b by at most e^(11m) nu_b.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One simultaneous reduction (OpenAI)
providers.scope: With probability at least 3/4, one mu_rho-random set W halves every capacity of a disjoint spread probability tree, keeps it nearly spread, and every new path union together with W contains an old one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tree covering (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If every level is sigma-spread and the capacities grow by factors of at least 16, a mu_r-random set with r = min{1, 16 e^50 sigma (1 + log_2 l_k)} contains some path union with probability at least 2/3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The spread lemma
providers.scope: A sigma-spread family of sets of size at most l has a member inside a mu_r-random set, r = min{1, 16 e^50 sigma (1 + log_2 l)}, with probability at least 2/3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Maximizers are small
providers.scope: With sigma = 128 p_E(n,H), every maximizer S of R(I, .) satisfies |S| < |I|/17.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Conditional extensions
providers.scope: Given a copy of H_(i-1), the edges added by a uniform extension to a copy of H_i form a 128 p_E(n,H)-spread random set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tree of extensions (OpenAI, after Tran)
providers.scope: There is a disjoint 128 p_E(n,H)-spread probability tree whose path unions are copies of H and whose capacities grow by factors of at least 16 up to at most e(H).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The second Kahn-Kalai conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Perfect matchings
providers.scope: log n/(3n) < p_c(n, PM_n) <= 2048 e^52 log_2 n / n for every even n >= 16.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Maximal truncation
providers.scope: If an admissible cutoff exists, the largest one, epsilon, leaves at most m/d masses above epsilon.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiscale selector estimate (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If F is not p-small, then with probability at least 9/10 a random colouring with colour probabilities 256^i p has one member H capturing lambda_H-mass at least 1 - 2^-i of the colours <= i, for every scale i.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Talagrand's conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: q_f(F) <= 25 * 512^4 q(F) for every nontrivial increasing family F, with the same budget 1/2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Global weight bound
providers.scope: The weights w(U) = b(U)^2 satisfy sum_U q^|U| w(U) <= mu_q(F).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Signed identity
providers.scope: If S is not covered by l members of F, then sum over U subset S of (-1)^|U| b(U)^l = 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Li's fractional cover
providers.scope: If mu_q(F) >= 1/2, the sets not covered by two members of F have a fractional cover of cost at most 1/2 at density q/2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two unions (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If mu_p(D) >= 1/2, the sets not covered by two members of D form a p/(50 * 512^4)-small family.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Covering lemma (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If |H| rho^r <= 2^(h+1) for an r-uniform family H, h >= 64, the sets containing 2^(12h) members of H have a cover of cost at most 3 * 2^-h at rho.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Thirty-two unions (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If mu_q(F) >= 1/2, the sets not covered by 32 members of F form a q/2^70-small family.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Talagrand's discrete convexity conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If mu_p(D) >= 1 - 2^-75, the sets not covered by 2^75 members of D form a p-small family.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Positive selector processes (Park-Pham)
providers.scope: For phi(S) = sup over t in T of sum_(i in S) t_i with nonnegative t, {phi >= 2^150 E phi} is p-small.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lower bounds for the integral threshold
providers.scope: q(H;n) >= 1/(n(n-1)) and q(H;n) >= n^(-2/d)/2 when H has degeneracy d.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Paley-Zygmund inequality
providers.scope: P(Z > theta E Z) >= (1 - theta)^2 (E Z)^2 / E Z^2 for Z >= 0 and 0 <= theta <= 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Compression after a random extension (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A family of sets of size at most s has a subfamily of at most ceil(2 r^-s) members that every set satisfying the family satisfies with probability at least 1/2 after a mu_r-random extension.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Neighbourhood transfer (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There is a typical family D with mu_r(D) >= 1 - 2^-75 such that bipartite graphs across a small set Y, with edges in a member of D and outside degrees at most s, have threshold at most 32 r.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bounded degeneracy and maximum degree (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Graphs with degeneracy at most s, maximum degree at most n^(2/3) and at most n/4 non-isolated vertices have threshold at most r when r^s >= n^(-1/100).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Small star forests (OpenAI, after Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand)
providers.scope: Star forests with at most n/100 non-isolated vertices have threshold at most 800 e^4 times their integral expectation threshold.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A typical cover of one copy
providers.scope: If q(H;n) < r and mu_r(D) >= 1 - 2^-75, some copy of H lies in the union of 2^75 members of D.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Degeneracy splitting (Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand)
providers.scope: A graph of degeneracy d is the edge-disjoint union of m graphs of degeneracy at most ceil(d/m).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Forests into star forests
providers.scope: Every forest is the edge-disjoint union of two star forests.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every graph H on at most n vertices splits into k pieces with p_c(H_i;n) <= L q(H;n), k and L absolute.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
